Benjamin Franklin - model: NOT_FOUND

Douglass practised by copying specific models (Webster's Italics, ship-yard letters, Master Thomas's handwriting) using chalk on fences, walls, and pavement, while Franklin practised through writing exercises done in his spare time at night, early morning, or Sundays alone in the printing-house; the evidence does not state what model Franklin used.

V2-dev-BOOK-en-T1-001.answer:
Faraday explains that the candle's heat creates an ascending current of air that cools the outer edges, keeping them solid while the interior melts. Points:

1. As air comes to the candle it moves upwards by the force of the current which the heat of the candle produces, cooling all the sides of the wax, tallow, or fuel, so the edge stays much cooler than the part within (evidence [2]).
2. The part within melts by the flame that runs down the wick as far as it can go before it is extinguished, but the part on the outside does not melt (evidence [2]).
3. This beautifully regular ascending current of air playing upon all sides keeps the exterior of the candle cool and forms the cup; if the current is one-sided, the cup becomes lop-sided and the fluid runs over in guttering (evidence [1]).
4. No fuel would serve for a candle which has not the property of giving this cup, except such fuel as the Irish bogwood, where the material itself is like a sponge and holds its own fuel (evidence [1], [4]).

V2-dev-BOOK-en-T2-001.answer:
Order was the hardest virtue for Franklin to acquire.

- Its number and precept: it is number 3 in his list, with the precept "Let all your things have their places; let each part of your business have its time" (Plan for Attaining Moral Perfection, list of virtues).
- Reason 1: he had not been early accustomed to it, having an exceeding good memory, so he was not sensible of the inconvenience of want of method (Order passage).
- Reason 2: as a master who must mix with the world, he often received people of business at their own hours, which interfered with it.
- Result: it cost him painful attention, his faults vexed him, he made little progress and had frequent relapses, and he remained "incorrigible with respect to Order," feeling the want of it even in old age.

V2-dev-BOOK-en-T2-002.answer:
Douglass learned to read in Baltimore through his mistress's initial teaching, Mr. Auld's prohibition, and then his own clever stratagems with white boys.

- Mrs. Auld first taught him: she kindly commenced to teach him the A, B, C, and then helped him spell words of three or four letters (Chapter VI).
- Mr. Auld found out and at once forbade her to continue, saying it was unlawful as well as unsafe to teach a slave to read (Chapter VI).
- His reasons: "If you give a nigger an inch, he will take an ell"; learning would spoil the best slave, forever unfit him to be a slave, make him unmanageable and of no value to his master, and make him discontented and unhappy (Chapter VI).
- Afterward, Douglass had no regular teacher, so he made friends of little white boys he met in the street and converted them into teachers, carrying his book on errands and trading bread for lessons, until he finally succeeded in learning to read (Chapter VII).

V2-dev-BOOK-en-T2-003.answer:
Faraday makes the water visible by placing a chimney over the burning candle: the moisture appearing on it is water produced from the candle by the action of the air upon its hydrogen (passage [1]).

He shows the presence of carbonic acid in two ways. First, the air coming out of the top of the chimney is nearly sufficient to blow out a light held to it, and will blow it quite out if opposed to the current (passage [1]); the same effect is later produced by gas from the candle itself, showing it is "caused by the very same substance that issued from the candle" (passage [5]). Second, he applies lime-water as a test: water impregnated with carbonic acid makes the lime-water turbid and white, which is proof of its presence (passage [3]); the lime combines with something from the candle to form a white powder exactly the same as whitening or chalk (passage [2]).

V2-dev-BOOK-en-T3-001.answer: Franklin's father made candles from tallow, which Faraday explains is the fat of the ox (Russian tallow, used for making dips). To turn it into stearin, the fat or tallow is first boiled with quick-lime to make a soap, and then the soap is decomposed by sulphuric acid, which takes away the lime and leaves the fat re-arranged as stearic acid, with glycerin produced at the same time; the oil is then pressed out, leaving the substance that is melted and cast into candles.

The contract may impose a maximum notice period of two months, the transition may last up to 30 calendar days (extendable to seven months if 30 days is technically unfeasible), and the provider may charge reduced switching charges until 12 January 2027.

- Article 25(2)(d): the maximum notice period for initiating the switching process shall not exceed two months.
- Article 25(2)(a): switching must occur without undue delay and no later than a mandatory maximum transitional period of 30 calendar days, initiated after the notice period, during which the contract remains applicable and the provider must assist and maintain business continuity.
- Article 25(4): if the 30-day period is technically unfeasible, the provider must notify the customer within 14 working days, justify this, and indicate an alternative transitional period not exceeding seven months, with service continuity ensured.
- Article 25(5): the customer has the right to extend the transitional period once for a period it considers more appropriate.
- Article 29(2)–(3): from 11 January 2024 to 12 January 2027, reduced switching charges may be imposed, capped at the provider's costs directly linked to the switching process; since March 2026 falls in this window, charges are allowed (full prohibition applies only from 12 January 2027, Article 29(1)).

V2-dev-LAW-en-T2-001.answer:
Yes, the Act reaches this conduct, under section 6 (bribery of foreign public officials).

- Section 6(1)–(2): a person is guilty if they bribe a foreign public official intending to influence them in that capacity and to obtain or retain business or an advantage in the conduct of business — winning a government contract satisfies this.
- Section 6(3): P bribes F by offering, promising or giving a financial or other advantage, where F is not permitted or required by the applicable written law to be influenced by it.
- Section 6(5): a French ministry official holds an administrative position of a country outside the United Kingdom, so is a "foreign public official".
- Section 12(2)–(3): although no act or omission forming part of the offence takes place in the UK, the acts done outside the UK would form part of such an offence if done in the UK, and proceedings may be taken anywhere in the UK.
- Section 12(4): the person has a "close connection" with the UK because they are a British citizen (paragraph (a)) at the time of the acts.

For a qualifying entity:

V2-dev-LAW-en-T3-001.answer:
Data Governance Act - Article 2(8): a data holder is a legal person, including public sector bodies and international organisations, or a natural person who is not a data subject with respect to the specific data in question, which has the right to grant access to or to share certain personal data or non-personal data in accordance with applicable Union or national law.
Data Act - Article 2(13): a data holder is a natural or legal person that has the right or obligation, in accordance with the Regulation, applicable Union law or national legislation adopted in accordance with Union law, to use and make available data, including, where contractually agreed, product data or related service data which it has retrieved or generated during the provision of a related service.

Both allow natural persons to be data holders, but the Data Governance Act excludes natural persons who are data subjects with respect to the specific data, whereas the Data Act has no such exclusion. The status is based on the right to grant access to or share data under the Data Governance Act, versus the right or obligation to use and make available data (including retrieved or generated product or related service data) under the Data Act.

V2-dev-LAW-en-T3-002.answer:
Bribery Act 2010, section 7 - version 2010 CHAPTER 23: a relevant commercial organisation is guilty of an offence if a person associated with it bribes another intending to obtain or retain business or an advantage for it; it is a defence to prove adequate procedures designed to prevent such conduct.
Modern Slavery Act 2015, section 54 - version 2015 CHAPTER 30: requires certain commercial organisations to prepare a slavery and human trafficking statement (approved and signed as set out in s.54(6)), publish it on their website with a prominent homepage link, or provide a copy within 30 days of a written request if they have no website; the Secretary of State may issue and must publish guidance about these duties.

The Bribery Act 2010 failure-to-prevent-bribery provision is expressly framed as a criminal offence ("guilty of an offence under this section"), with an adequate-procedures defence. The Modern Slavery Act 2015 evidence describes the statement as a transparency duty enforced through publication and guidance requirements, but the passages provided do not state that failing to produce a statement is a criminal offence or specify any penalty, so the two are not directly comparable on punishment from this evidence.

V2-dev-RPT-en-T2-001.answer:
Zalando changed Zalando Plus from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system, and it recognised accruals for reimbursing Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025.

- The programme was evolved in 2024 into a points-based system rewarding customer loyalty, moving from a paid membership to a free-to-join model (Group strategy; Key intangible resources; Accounting policies).
- Points earned unlock four benefit levels, with perks like birthday vouchers and exclusive events; the new approach was tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout in 2025 (Group strategy; Foreword).
- Under the accounting policies, the awards create a separate performance obligation providing a material right to customers (Accounting policies).
- Among other current non-financial liabilities, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" (Notes 9.–26.).

V2-dev-RPT-en-T2-002.answer:
Delivery Hero treats the two periods differently: the pre-August 2021 model risk is deemed probable, so provisions are recognized, while the post-August 2021 model risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed only as a contingency. Glovo decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain from 2025.

- Provisions are reflected for risks in Spain relating to the model operated by Glovo until August 2021, as it is more likely than not that the risk materializes (Strategic Risks, [1]).
- For Glovo Spain after August 2021, the rider risk is deemed possible but not probable and is disclosed as a contingency, with a contingent liability of €440 to 770 million for the Spanish social security investigation into the model since August 2021 (Strategic Risks [1]; Auditor's Report [2]; Contingencies [3]).
- No provision was recognized for the post-2021 model because reclassification by Spanish courts was assessed as not probable, though the courier fleet was reclassified to employee status in January 2025 (Contingencies, [3]).
- In December 2024, Glovo's management decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain effective 2025 to avoid further legal uncertainties, while Glovo will defend the self-employed status through all available instances and continue cooperating with Spanish authorities (Strategic Risks [4]; CEO letter [6]).

Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension: €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT), paid in advance with a capital injection.
Turkcell - 2G licence extension: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes), paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (TRY 1.7 billion) in 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million, TRY 1.1 billion) in April 2024, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.

Both agreed to the same €120 million fee (excluding VAT) for extension to 30 April 2029, but Vodafone Turkey paid the fee in advance via a capital injection, whereas Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira over 2023–2025.
